explanation: A two-table join should match the foreign key in `Book` to the referenced key in `Author`, which is `b.author_id = a.author_id`. Option A does that correctly. Option B does not join to `Author` at all, option C joins on unrelated columns, and option D creates a Cartesian product because it has no join condition.

options.text:
```sql
SELECT b.title, a.author_name
FROM Book b
JOIN Author a
  ON b.author_id = a.author_id;
```

```sql
SELECT b.title, a.author_name
FROM Book b
JOIN Author a
  ON b.book_id = a.author_id;
```

```sql
SELECT b.title, a.author_name
FROM Book b, Author a;
```

prompt: A bookstore tracks authors in `Author(author_id, author_name)` and books in `Book(book_id, title, author_id)`. Every book has exactly one author. Which query correctly returns each book title with its author name?
reviewConcept: Join related tables by matching a foreign key to its referenced key.
